body: Soft context compression condenses a context into a few memory tokens that a frozen LLM consumes in place of the raw text, but existing compressors fix the compression ratio at training and inference: each deployed ratio requires a separately trained model, and the chosen ratio is applied uniformly to all inputs, whose actual needs vary drastically. We propose FlexComp, a method-agnostic framework that decouples the ratio from both training and deployment: Matryoshka-style training samples the memory budget K per instance, turning one model into an any-ratio compressor, and the budget is then chosen per input by: (1) confidence-based cascade routing or (2) a lightweight learned K predictor. Across ICAE, 500xCompressor, and SAC on MRQA, a single FlexComp model matches separately trained fixed-ratio specialists with minimal degradation. Cascade routing preserves over 98% of the mildest ratio's accuracy at up to 266x average compression; the K predictor, in a single compression-decoding pass, reaches 158-236x within 0.7 F1 of the mildest ratio. At serving-scale batch sizes, the K predictor cuts context KV cache by 50% and improves decoding throughput by 47%.
